response.rationale: C1 is the most complete: it names inferior MI with aneurysm and adds the post-infarction temporal qualifier, supported by the inferior aneurysm, inferior akinesis, and RCA thrombus. R2 is the same core diagnosis but lacks the temporal qualifier and raw support spans. R1 captures coronary obstruction but omits the MI/aneurysm; R5 only cites hypertension as a risk factor.

rejected.why: Coronary angiography supports underlying coronary artery disease, but this is not the full diagnosis and omits the inferior MI and aneurysm formation.
Untreated hypertension is only a risk factor; there is no raw evidence of hypertensive heart disease and it does not explain the infarction or aneurysm.
